title: POC weekly - connection path degradation simulation and rollback
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on a simulated connection-path degradation test, validating fallback routing and rollback procedures for Redwood Private in CardinalThera's VPC. Action items include running a staged rollback rehearsal, sharing an updated runbook, and scheduling a telemetry deep-dive with Cardinal's SREs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake, Priya Nair, Marta Liu (Redwood) — Samir Patel, Elena Gomez, Marcus Lee, Tina O'Connor, Ravi Menon (CardinalThera)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call, then we'll kick off with the degradation sim we ran late yesterday.
[00:08] Samir: Yep, we're here. Appreciate you running this; we had a couple questions from the team about the fallback timing.
[00:15] Priya: Cool, quick agenda — 1) what we observed in the sim 2) telemetry anomalies 3) rollback rehearsal plan 4) next steps. If that works we'll go in order.
[00:27] Elena: works for us.
[00:30] Priya: Alright, first, recap: we intentionally injected 30% packet loss on our inter-subnet egress path to simulate a path degradation. The goal was to validate Redwood's smart routing fallback to an alternative region and verify KV-cache warmup and prefix caching behavior during the switch.
[00:52] Marcus: Right, summary on our side — we saw the service degrade around t+28s after the fault injection, p50 latency spiked from 60ms to 420ms and p95 went over 1.2s. A handful of requests timed out; we had 0.6% errors.
[01:10] Priya: That aligns with what our runtime telemetry showed. We detected the increased tail, then triggered the fallback policy which routes to the secondary region after the cluster misses the latency SLO for three consecutive evaluation windows (~30s total). The reroute itself happened around t+33s.
[01:30] Elena: We noticed an odd pause where the KV cache didn't seem to populate right away after the route switch. Could be our side — NAT session stickiness maybe?
[01:41] Priya: We saw that too. There's a small window where the runtime rehydrates KV entries; if requests hit different worker pods before the cache warms, you see cold token penalties. In the sim the TTLs were short so it was more pronounced.
[01:55] Ravi: I also saw a spike in our egress gateway CPU at the same time which might be causing packet queuing and contributing to the delay.
[02:04] Marcus: I can share the egress cpu metrics after this meeting. We were surprised by the NAT translation churn once sessions moved to the other AZ.
[02:13] Priya: Great, that leads into telemetry — we captured both runtime and CardinalNet traces. One caveat: the auto-transcription mis-tagged some of the fields, the trace IDs are in the deck link but the mapping file has a few entries labeled as "K V cash miss" which is wrong — it should be KV cache miss.
[02:29] Jordan: (laughs) the transcription gremlins strike again. But yes, link is in chat: "sim-degrad-20270802-traces.csv".
[02:36] Samir: On remediation, our priority is a deterministic rollback path. We don't want to rely on a fully automated region failover in prod without a rehearsed manual rollback.
[02:47] Marta: Totally — our opinionated rollback is designed to be a staged three-step: 1) shift a small weight to fallback region, 2) if metrics improve, do a full cutover, 3) otherwise run kernel roll-forward or rollback to previous runtime. The idea is to avoid flip-flopping.
[03:06] Tina: From security, we need the runbook to include exact audit log retention locations and the SAML session behavior when rerouting. Also, will keys be re-negotiated across regions?
[03:17] Priya: Keys are negotiated per connection; if you route to a different region the TLS session will terminate and renegotiate — that's expected. We don't re-key application-level data via KMS automatically, but we maintain the same KMS policy; cross-region KMS access depends on your config.
[03:33] Elena: That's an important callout. For PCI/sensitive workloads we may need cross-region key restrictions.
[03:41] Jordan: Noted. We'll flag the KMS cross-region behavior in the runbook.
[03:46] Priya: Back to the simulation: we also intentionally toggled the kernel compatibility flag to a newer quant-friendly path to see if quantized kernels impacted latency during the fallback. The newer kernel had slightly lower throughput on cold start but better steady-state cpu efficiency.
[04:03] Marcus: So the kernel change could have exacerbated the slow KV rehydration during the cold window?
[04:08] Priya: It appears so. The quant path uses a different memory layout which affects initial KV lookups on some architectures; on AMD hosts in particular we saw longer cold miss penalties.
[04:20] Samir: Our on-prem cluster has a mixed fleet — some older cards. That might explain variability. If the runtime picks the quant kernel automatically, we need clear rules for pinned kernels per pool.
[04:31] Priya: Absolutely. We can add a policy: pin kernel variants per node pool, and have the router avoid routing to incompatible pools during fallbacks.
[04:40] Ravi: One behavioral quirk we noticed: when the fallback policy activated it triggered a burst of cache replays from our app because we saw many retry loops. Client retry backoff settings amplified the rehydration storm.
[04:55] Elena: We did have retries configured aggressively to preserve user experience, so that makes sense. Maybe throttle retries during a detected fallback window.
[05:03] Priya: Good idea. We can provide a recommended client retry strategy: exponential backoff with jitter and a short idempotent-safe window during failovers.
[05:12] Jordan: Ok, let's talk rollback rehearsal specifics. We propose a dry run next Tuesday where Redwood initiates a staged rollback in a lower environment that mirrors your prod network (subnets, NATs). Priya, you want to lead the rehearsal?
[05:25] Priya: Yeah, I can. Proposed steps: pre-check (verify telemetry ingestion, snapshot config), inject degradation, observe failover, initiate staged rollback, validate KV cache and tracing, then collect artifacts. We'll timebox to 90 minutes.
[05:39] Marcus: That works. What do you need from our side to mirror the network?
[05:43] Priya: We need a topology diagram, access to a staging NAT/gateway or a scoped pcap export, and the list of node pools with GPU types. Small ask: a user that can pull CloudWatch or equivalent egress metrics for the window.
[05:57] Marcus: I'll assemble those. Expect a diagram and node pool list by tomorrow EOD.
[06:02] Samir: On the runbook execution, I want a clear abort condition — if errors exceed 1% or p95 stays worse than baseline+500ms after 5 minutes, abort and rollback. Can we codify that?
[06:13] Priya: Yes, we can put exact SLO thresholds in the runbook. Our tooling can add annotations to the dashboard to show the abort thresholds.
[06:21] Tina: For compliance, we'll need the full audit trail of who triggered the rollback and the exact configuration diffs. Does Redwood provide immutable logs for runbook operations?
[06:31] Jordan: We do. In Redwood Private, the control plane can stream audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket or to your SIEM; logs are append-only and we can include runbook step records with checksums.
[06:44] Tina: Great. Also need to confirm RBAC roles so only two approvers can execute a rollback in prod.
[06:51] Marta: We support role gates. We'll include a sample RBAC YAML in the deliverables.
[06:57] Ravi: Quick note — during the sim we observed that the health-checker flagged a subset of pods as "unready" which delayed routing decisions. The health probe timings might need tuning.
[07:09] Priya: Good callout. Health probe periods and failure thresholds can be tuned; we don't want overly sensitive checks in the middle of a transient egress blip.
[07:19] Elena: Another item — curious about session stickiness: if we fail over mid-session, do you terminate existing sessions or let them drain?
[07:28] Priya: We try to drain. The router marks nodes as draining and shifts new requests. But if NAT mappings expire, you do see a hard cut. That's why NAT session timeouts and preferred ephemeral port ranges matter.
[07:40] Marcus: We can increase NAT timeout for the staging test to observe impact.
[07:44] Jordan: Good. On documentation, we'll produce: 1) rollback runbook 2) kernel compatibility matrix per node type 3) telemetry mapping file (with corrected labels) 4) recommended client retry patterns. Expect those by Friday.
[07:59] Priya: And we'll include a small test harness script you can run to reproduce the sim locally that toggles egress at the subnet level. It uses iptables rules in staging and collects traces to the shared S3.
[08:11] Samir: Perfect. A few smaller questions — did the sim exercise on-prem private links (MPLS) or only cloud egress?
[08:19] Priya: This run was cloud egress only. We can extend to private links if you can provide a lab endpoint; the behavior often varies due to jitter and buffer sizes on MPLS.
[08:29] Samir: We can do that in the rehearsal if needed.
[08:33] Tina: Regarding encryption, if we route across regions, will the traffic traverse public internet or remain within private peering?
[08:42] Jordan: It depends on your VPC peering/VPN setup. Redwood routes over the path you provide; we never force a public egress unless that's the only available path. We recommend private inter-region peering for sensitive workloads.
[08:56] Marcus: One more ops note — can Redwood provide a checksum diff of the runtime binary used in each region? We want to ensure bitwise parity.
[09:04] Priya: Yes; we can share binary checksums and container image digests per deployed version in the runbook artifacts.
[09:12] Elena: Great.
[09:15] Jordan: Ok final quick recap: Redwood will send runbook, kernel matrix, telemetry mapping, and test harness by 2027-08-05. Cardinal provides topology and node pool list by 2027-08-04. We schedule a 90-minute rollback rehearsal next Tuesday; Priya to propose time.
[09:33] Samir: That's right. Also, we'd like Redwood to include a short checklist for security review so our auditors have a clear entry.
[09:43] Tina: And please include sample audit logs and RBAC YAML.
[09:47] Jordan: Will do. Anything else?
[09:50] Marcus: Just one quick ask — can we get a quick one-off benchmark showing quant kernel performance on an older GPU type you mentioned? Even a 5-10 minute perf run would help decisioning.
[09:59] Priya: Yep I can run that and share numbers in the rehearsal artifacts.
[10:03] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and calendar invite for rehearsal.
[10:10] Elena: Thanks all, talk soon.
[10:12] Meeting ends.
